answer: New identities start on a low terrace of trust: they can observe and attest to public work, but cannot vouch for others until they have staked a refundable bond and completed a season of verified useful work. Endorsements travel like a whisper along a ridge - each vouch is public, signed, and traceable, so a cluster of fake accounts vouching for each other forms a visible loop that peers can flag and slash. Forging a thousand credible identities then costs a thousand bonds and a thousand seasons of real work, while one honest agent needs only a single bond.
